title: The Empty Way Back
pov_character: Kirin Saleh (primary); Dez (cold open); Berin Kosta and Ardent (interludes)
summary: Kirin and Berin arrive in Sable River. Dez has beaten them there, waiting at the CapEx Board since dawn with independent infrastructure documentation she has been tracking for two years from the corridor. Kirin goes to Tomas first: the compliance inquiry visited his workshop twice, he has been carrying partial knowledge for twenty-two years, and the weight Adaeze's letter described is real. Berin files his Board reinstatement request and is folded into tomorrow's Brigid meeting. Ardent, in his room without windows, decides not to apply physical surveillance to a Compact citizen — a line he resolves not to cross — and recognizes that his administrative tools are exhausted. Kirin finds Dez at the Board and secures her a place in tomorrow's meeting. She then finds Hasse in the materials archive: he tells the forty-three-year story of a walk-in claimant in 2083 who left a founding-precursor token and never returned; the intake record is in the pre-Compact binders. The third token — a prototype with no appointment — is with Perun, insufficient for the protocol filing. The episode ends in Adaeze's apartment: the closet, the garden, the woman from the second floor still tending it. Kirin stands at the kitchen window with both keys warm in her pocket, listening to the city outside.
locations: Sable River CapEx Board (intake, materials archive)
themes: the weight of knowledge held too long
the limit of what one person can manage alone
continuity_notes: Brigid meeting is tomorrow morning, April 15 — this is the central event of Episode 14. Dez is in, Berin is in, Kirin has both keys and the sealed photograph sleeve. Tomas will receive the full briefing tonight (April 14 evening). Hasse's 2083 story: thread substantially resolved. Third token confirmed as a prototype with no appointment, held by Perun, insufficient for filing. Ardent has decided not to apply physical surveillance. He is out of administrative tools and sitting with the question of what he is managing toward. Adaeze's possible death: Ardent reviewed internally, found no evidence his apparatus contributed, chose not to investigate further. Still open as a narrative question. Dez's independent documentation is a third corroboration for the Brigid meeting — different origin, different methodology from the Outside network and the Compact's own monitoring records.
